Amidst the din, members of the ruling alliance, which includes the National Conference (NC), Congress, and CPI(M), stood to demand the immediate restoration of Jammu and Kashmir’s statehood on September 21, 2026 | Photo Credit: ANI

The ruling alliance in Jammu and Kashmir, led by the National Conference (NC), on Monday (September 21, 2026) pitched for the restoration of Statehood on the first day of the autumn session of the Assembly, with the Opposition BJP cornering the Omar Abdullah government over the governance issues.

Several NC, Congress and CPI(M) Legislators raised the issue of Statehood. It sparked a strong reaction from BJP legislators, who stormed into the well of the House and raised slogans against the government. The legislators from the treasury benches and the opposition benches jostled against one another to register their protests.

“All legislators, irrespective of political affiliations, should jointly press the Government of India to fulfil its repeated commitment to restore full Statehood to Jammu and Kashmir. The legislature itself is disempowered, and thereby citizens feel disappointed,” said CPI legislator M.Y. Tarigami, who is part of the ruling alliance.

Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee president and legislator Tariq Hameed Karra accused the BJP of “disrupting Question Hour to divert attention from Statehood”. “The BJP shied away from responding to issues such as Statehood, paper leaks etc. Instead, the BJP disrupted the proceedings,” said Mr. Karra.

BJP legislator and Leader of the Opposition Sunil Sharma cornered the Omar Abdullah government over a slew of governance issues. Mr. Sharma highlighted the pending issues of regularisation of National Health Mission employees, a 6.83% hike in electricity tariffs, regularisation of the services of daily wagers and Anganwadi workers.

“The Omar government is running away from people’s issues, but the Opposition must hold him accountable. Mr. Abdullah wants to evade, but the BJP will not let him run and will fulfil its duty with integrity,” said Mr. Sharma.

Mr. Abdullah, in a post on X, said, “The Assembly will provide an opportunity for meaningful debate, constructive deliberations and discussion on issues concerning the welfare and aspirations of our people.” Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary also said the Ministers were “here to give answers on any issue”.

Meanwhile, the Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) legislators Waheed-ur-Rehman Parra and Aga Syed Muntazir Mehdi said the House was “deliberately” disrupted to “ensure that critical issues such as contentious reservation policy, protesting intern doctors, NHM employees, and daily wagers are not addressed”. “A community that constitutes 60% of the population has been reduced to a mere 14% share in the reservation matrix,” said Mr. Mehdi.

Mr. Parra sought the government’s attention on youth, “as Jammu and Kashmir has a 32% unemployment rate”. “This is the first time in the history of India that you are punishing the meritorious population. You give 30% opportunities to nearly 70% of the population. A flawed reservation policy was created here due to political reasons, and there is a need to revisit it and rationalise it,” said Mr. Parra.

He also highlighted the issue of the fertility rate, which had dropped to 1.4 children per woman in Jammu and Kashmir. “It is the lowest in India. Late marriages, mass voluntary bachelorhood, rising divorce, crushing financial pressure, and rising infertility are gutting the next generation before it is even born,” said Mr. Parra.
